entries.name: Asian Development Bank - Japan Scholarship Program (ADB-JSP)
entries.provider: Asian Development Bank, funded by the Government of Japan
entries.fields: Economics, management, science and technology and other development-related fields at designated institutions in Japan, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Thailand, Hong Kong, India, Pakistan, Philippines, USA (Hawaii)
entries.eligibility: National of an ADB borrowing member country eligible for Japanese ODA (Cambodia qualifies); bachelor's degree with excellent record; at least 2 years full-time professional experience after the degree; under 35 years old; proficient in English; not living/working outside home country; no dual citizenship of a developed country; must return home after study.
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodians apply directly to one of the roughly 25 designated institutions (e.g. AIT Thailand, University of Tokyo, Hitotsubashi, Kyoto, Nagoya, Tsukuba, IUJ, Ritsumeikan APU, East-West Center, NUS, Melbourne, ANU, Auckland etc.) and indicate they wish to be considered for ADB-JSP; the institution endorses candidates to ADB. Living in Cambodia at time of application is required.
entries.deadline_note: Deadlines set by each designated institution, typically about six months before the academic term (many fall between December and May); no direct application to ADB.
entries.language_req: English proficiency required by the host university (typically IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 80+)

entries.name: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP)
entries.provider: World Bank, funded by the Government of Japan
entries.fields: Development-related master's programs at participating universities (preferred programs in the US, Europe, Japan, Australia, Africa and Asia; and partner programs in Japan)
entries.eligibility: National of a World Bank member developing country (Cambodia is eligible); bachelor's degree earned at least 3 years before the application deadline; at least 3 years of paid development-related work experience; currently employed in paid development work; not a dual citizen of a developed country; not a World Bank Group staff member or relative; admitted unconditionally to a participating master's program
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodians apply directly online during the two application windows after securing admission to a participating program; Cambodia is on the eligible developing-country list
entries.deadline_note: Two windows each year: window 1 opens in January and closes late February; window 2 opens in March and closes about mid-May; partner-program (Japan) applications go through the universities
entries.language_req: English proficiency required by the host university

entries.name: Japan-IMF Scholarship Program for Asia (JISPA)
entries.provider: International Monetary Fund, funded by the Government of Japan
entries.fields: Macroeconomics, public finance, economics, public policy and related fields at partner universities (GRIPS, Hitotsubashi, University of Tokyo, International University of Japan)
entries.eligibility: Citizen of an eligible Asian country including Cambodia; government official (central bank, ministry of finance, planning, statistics or similar) with strong potential for a policy-making career; bachelor's degree with strong academic record; under 40 preferred; strong English; must return to government service after study
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodia is on the JISPA eligible country list; candidates are typically nominated through their government employer (e.g. National Bank of Cambodia, Ministry of Economy and Finance) and apply online to the IMF for the partnership track
entries.deadline_note: Partnership-track applications usually open in October and close in early December each year for study starting the following October
entries.language_req: TOEFL iBT or IELTS as required by partner universities

entries.name: Obama Foundation Scholars Program
entries.provider: Obama Foundation with Columbia University and the University of Chicago
entries.fields: Columbia track: one-year non-degree leadership program at Columbia University; University of Chicago track: scholarship for final-year master's students at Harris (public policy), Crown Family School (social work) or Booth (business)
entries.eligibility: Emerging leaders from any country with several years (typically 3-10) of demonstrated impact in civic or public work; commitment to return home to advance their work; for Chicago track, must have been admitted to and be in the final year of a qualifying UChicago master's program
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodians may apply directly online; the Chicago track requires separate admission to a University of Chicago master's program
entries.deadline_note: Columbia track usually opens around December and closes in January/February; Chicago track applications close in spring; 2026-27 cohorts have been selected, so next cycle is for 2027-28
entries.language_req: English proficiency (TOEFL/IELTS for non-native speakers)

entries.name: Maurice R. Greenberg World Fellows Program (Yale World Fellows)
entries.provider: Yale University (Jackson School of Global Affairs)
entries.fields: Four-month mid-career global leadership fellowship (non-degree)
covers: travel to and from New Haven
entries.eligibility: Mid-career professionals (typically 5-20 years of experience, usually aged early 30s to early 40s) with a record of leadership in any sector; fluent in English; citizens of any country outside the US (US citizens eligible only in limited cases); must be available for the full residential period (August to December)
entries.cambodia_note: Open to Cambodian leaders; apply directly online to Yale, no nomination needed
entries.deadline_note: Applications usually open in September/October and close in early December each year for the following August-December cohort
entries.language_req: Fluent English (no formal test)

entries.name: East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship
entries.fields: Any master's or doctoral field offered by the University of Hawai'i at Manoa, with emphasis on Asia-Pacific issues
covers: tuition and fees (partial or full depending on funding)
entries.eligibility: Citizens of Asia-Pacific countries (including Cambodia) and the US; must apply for and be admitted to a graduate program at the University of Hawai'i at Manoa; strong academic record; commitment to community building and Asia-Pacific engagement
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodians are in the Asia-Pacific eligible group; apply online to the East-West Center and separately to the University of Hawai'i
entries.deadline_note: Application opens in August and closes 1 December each year for study starting the following August
entries.language_req: TOEFL/IELTS as required by the University of Hawai'i

entries.name: JICA Scholarship Program – SDGs Global Leader Program (Cambodia)
entries.fields: Development-related fields at Japanese universities including engineering, ICT, agriculture, health, environment, urban development, economics and public policy
entries.eligibility: Cambodian national, usually under 40 (some cycles under 45), bachelor's degree, employed in a Cambodian government agency, public institution, university or private/civil organization relevant to development, with employer endorsement and commitment to return after graduation
entries.cambodia_note: Announced and screened by the JICA Cambodia Office in Phnom Penh; candidates are shortlisted by JICA and must separately obtain admission from a partner Japanese university.
entries.deadline_note: Call usually issued once a year (recent cycles around July–October) for enrolment in Japan the following autumn or spring; check the JICA Cambodia office announcement for the current cycle.
entries.language_req: English (university may require TOEFL/IELTS); Japanese not required for English-taught programs

entries.name: Ajinomoto Scholarship for ASEAN+ONE
entries.provider: The Ajinomoto Foundation / Ajinomoto Co., Inc.
entries.fields: Food science, nutrition, biosciences, agricultural and life sciences and related fields at designated Japanese universities (University of Tokyo, Kyoto, Nagoya, Ochanomizu, Kagawa Nutrition and others)
covers: monthly stipend (approx. JPY 150,000 as research student, JPY 180,000 as master's student)
entrance examination, admission and tuition fees
entries.eligibility: National of one of the eligible ASEAN countries listed by the foundation (Cambodia has been listed in recent cycles; verify); under 35; bachelor's degree with strong grades; intends to enrol as a research student and then a master's course at a designated university; able to attend interview in home country; not already receiving another scholarship
entries.cambodia_note: Application goes to the Ajinomoto Foundation / Ajinomoto Cambodia country contact and to the chosen Japanese university; typically one award per country per year.
entries.deadline_note: Applications usually accepted in the first quarter of the year (roughly January–March) for enrolment the following year; confirm the current cycle on the foundation page.
entries.language_req: English (TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent) or Japanese depending on the host laboratory

entries.name: Rotary Yoneyama Scholarship for Overseas Applicants
entries.fields: any
covers: monthly stipend (approx. JPY 100,000 undergraduate; JPY 140,000 master's/doctoral)
entries.eligibility: Non-Japanese national living outside Japan who has been accepted (or is applying) to a degree program at a Japanese university that participates in the overseas-applicant scheme; age limits generally under 45; good academic record; interest in Rotary exchange; cannot hold another major scholarship concurrently
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodians apply through the participating Japanese university's international office (the university recommends candidates to the foundation); there is no embassy step in Phnom Penh.
entries.deadline_note: Universities collect applications in autumn (around September–November) for April enrolment and in spring for October enrolment; exact dates vary by university.
entries.language_req: Japanese or English as required by the host university

entries.name: Honjo International Scholarship Foundation – Scholarship for Foreign Students in Japan
entries.fields: any (STEM, business and social sciences all eligible)
covers: monthly stipend of about JPY 150,000–200,000 depending on program length
entries.eligibility: Non-Japanese national planning to enrol full-time in a master's or doctoral program at a Japanese graduate school (or already enrolled); age under about 30 for master's and under 35 for doctoral at enrolment; not receiving another scholarship of comparable value; intends to contribute to home country
entries.cambodia_note: Applied for online directly with the foundation from Cambodia or from Japan; no embassy or ministry nomination required.
entries.deadline_note: Main application window is typically September to October each year for enrolment the following April; a smaller spring round has existed for October enrolment. Verify current cycle.
entries.language_req: Japanese or English as required by the host graduate school

entries.name: Otsuka Toshimi Scholarship
entries.fields: Medicine, pharmacy, nutrition/food science, physical education and business administration at Japanese universities
covers: annual scholarship of about JPY 1.4–2.0 million (paid monthly)
entries.eligibility: Privately financed international student of any nationality already enrolled (or accepted) at a Japanese university or graduate school in an eligible field; good academic record; financial need; not receiving other major scholarships
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodian students apply through the international student office of their Japanese university, which forwards the application to the foundation.
entries.deadline_note: Applications usually collected by universities between February and mid-April each year for the academic year starting in April.
entries.language_req: Japanese or English as required by the host university

entries.name: JASSO Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students
entries.provider: Japan Student Services Organization (JASSO), Government of Japan
entries.fields: any
covers: monthly stipend (approx. JPY 48,000 for university/graduate students; JPY 30,000–40,000 for Japanese-language and preparatory courses)
entries.eligibility: Privately financed international student of any nationality enrolled full-time at a Japanese university, graduate school, junior college, college of technology, specialized training college or Japanese-language institution; good academic performance; not receiving another scholarship above a set amount; also a reservation scheme for high scorers in the EJU exam
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodians cannot apply directly: the Japanese school nominates enrolled students to JASSO. Candidates sitting the EJU (Examination for Japanese University Admission) can also apply for the reservation program through the exam.
entries.deadline_note: Schools collect applications around April–May for the academic year; reservation program applies at EJU registration (June and November sittings).
entries.language_req: none beyond the school's own admission requirements

entries.name: Hitachi Global Foundation Scholarship (Hitachi Scholarship)
entries.fields: Science and engineering fields (including environment, energy, ICT, materials, life sciences) for doctoral study or research at Japanese universities
entries.eligibility: Young full-time faculty members or researchers at universities in the foundation's designated Southeast Asian countries (Cambodia has been listed in recent calls; verify), under about 35, master's degree, nominated by their home university, planning doctoral study or short research stay in Japan and return afterwards
entries.cambodia_note: Nomination comes from the Cambodian home university (e.g. RUPP, ITC) to the foundation; individuals cannot apply without institutional endorsement.
entries.deadline_note: Annual call usually opens in autumn with a deadline around November–December for study starting the following autumn.
entries.language_req: English (TOEFL/IELTS) or Japanese as required by the host laboratory

entries.name: Huawei Seeds for the Future – Cambodia
entries.provider: Huawei Technologies (Cambodia) Co., Ltd. with the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications
entries.fields: ICT: 5G, cloud, AI, cybersecurity, digital economy, plus leadership and cultural modules
covers: all program costs including travel and accommodation for the on-site component (when held in China)
entries.eligibility: Cambodian citizen enrolled as an undergraduate (usually 2nd year or above) or master's student in ICT-related majors at a Cambodian university, generally aged 18–30, good academic standing and English; selected by written test and interview
entries.cambodia_note: Applications are run locally by Huawei Cambodia together with the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications and partner universities; announcements appear on the Huawei Cambodia and MPTC Facebook pages.
entries.deadline_note: Held once a year; Cambodian recruitment usually runs around May–August with the program in the second half of the year. Verify current cycle.
entries.language_req: English (working proficiency; no fixed test score)

entries.name: GitHub Student Developer Pack
entries.fields: Software development and computing (tools, cloud credits, courses)
covers: cloud and hosting credits from partner companies
free courses and certifications from partners
entries.eligibility: Student aged 13+ enrolled in a degree- or diploma-granting course at an accredited institution anywhere in the world; must verify with school email, student ID or enrolment document
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodian students verify directly on the GitHub Education site; a school-issued document is accepted if the university has no student email domain.
entries.deadline_note: Rolling; apply any time and renew verification annually.
entries.language_req: none

entries.name: Coursera Financial Aid
entries.fields: any (individual courses, specializations and professional certificates from partner universities and companies)
covers: waived or reduced course fee for the specific course applied for
access to graded assignments and certificate
entries.eligibility: Any learner worldwide who cannot afford the fee; separate application per course with income statement and short essays; not available for degrees or some MasterTrack programs
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodians apply from the course page ('Financial aid available'); no local partner needed.
entries.deadline_note: Rolling; decisions usually take up to 15 days after applying.
entries.language_req: none

entries.name: edX Financial Assistance
entries.fields: any (verified-track courses from partner universities)
covers: up to 90% discount on the verified certificate fee for eligible courses
entries.eligibility: Learners of any country who demonstrate financial need; per-course application with a short statement; excludes some programs (e.g. MicroMasters, professional certificates, degrees) and learners in sanctioned countries
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodians apply online through the edX learner dashboard for each course; no local step.
entries.deadline_note: Rolling; apply before the course's upgrade deadline.
entries.language_req: none

entries.name: Harvard College Need-Based Financial Aid (need-blind for international students)
entries.fields: any
covers: books and personal expenses (need-based, grant only, no loans)
entries.eligibility: Admitted first-year undergraduates of any nationality; aid is 100% need-based (no merit). Families earning under USD 100,000 pay nothing; families up to USD 200,000 get at least full tuition covered. Admission is need-blind for foreign citizens.
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodian applicants apply directly online through the Common Application/Coalition; financial aid is awarded on exactly the same basis as for US students. No embassy or ministry involvement; submit CSS Profile (Harvard code 3434) plus translated parent income documents.
entries.deadline_note: Applications open in August; Restrictive Early Action deadline 1 November, Regular Decision deadline early January each year; CSS Profile due at the same time as the admission application.
entries.language_req: English; TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo not required but may be submitted

entries.name: MIT Need-Based Financial Aid for International Undergraduates (need-blind, full need)
entries.fields: any (MIT undergraduate programs, STEM-focused)
covers: books and personal expenses (need-based MIT Scholarship)
entries.eligibility: Admitted undergraduates of any citizenship; MIT is need-blind and meets 100% of demonstrated financial need for all four years. Aid amount depends on family finances via CSS Profile and parental income documents.
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodian nationals apply directly through the MIT online application; international students use the same aid process as domestic students (CSS Profile plus parent income documentation). No government nomination.
entries.deadline_note: Application opens in August; Early Action deadline 1 November, Regular Action deadline early January; CSS Profile due mid-February for aid.
entries.language_req: English; TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo/Cambridge optional but recommended for non-native speakers

entries.name: Yale College Need-Based Financial Aid for International Students (need-blind)
entries.fields: any
covers: travel to and from campus twice a year
books and personal expenses (grant-based, no loans)
entries.eligibility: Admitted Yale College students of any citizenship; awards are 100% need-based and meet full demonstrated need without loans. Awards account for the economic difference between the US and the student's home country.
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodian students apply directly online (Common App/Coalition/QuestBridge) and submit the CSS Profile; financial need does not affect admission for any applicant anywhere in the world.
entries.deadline_note: Applications open in August; Single-Choice Early Action deadline 1 November, Regular Decision deadline early January each year.
entries.language_req: English; TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo recommended if English is not the language of instruction

entries.name: Princeton University Need-Based Financial Aid for International Students (need-blind)
entries.fields: any
covers: books and personal expenses (100% grant, no loans)
entries.eligibility: Admitted undergraduates of any nationality; Princeton is need-blind for all applicants including international students and meets 100% of demonstrated need with grants. Entirely need-based, no academic or athletic merit scholarships.
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodian applicants apply directly online; the same aid application (Princeton Financial Aid Application) and full-need policy apply to international students. No embassy or ministry process.
entries.deadline_note: Applications open in August; Single-Choice Early Action deadline 1 November, Regular Decision deadline 1 January each year.
entries.language_req: English; TOEFL/IELTS/PTE required unless English is the primary language of instruction

entries.name: Amherst College Need-Based Financial Aid for International Students (need-blind)
entries.fields: any (liberal arts)
covers: travel allowance (scholarships and grants; no loans packaged)
entries.eligibility: Admitted international students who apply for need-based aid; Amherst is need-blind for international applicants and meets 100% of calculated need. Need is met first with a work-study expectation and the rest by scholarship.
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodian nationals apply directly via the Common Application and submit the CSS Profile with parent income documents; treated identically to domestic applicants for aid.
entries.deadline_note: Applications open in August; Early Decision deadline 1 November (ED II around 1 January), Regular Decision deadline early January each year.
entries.language_req: English; TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo expected for non-native English speakers
